decision.title: CLDR tailorings and the CLDR root for UCA collations (packet 7.15b)
decision.summary: UCA collations take CLDR's root table and per-language tailorings, read from the host as CLDR files under urn:sxml:collation-data:, with the DUCET as the fallback root.

body.p: , after , , , , , , , . Replaces 's "lang other than the root languages and reorder are not honoured" and its root order.

item.p: One resource kind, CLDR paths (no COLLATION_TAILORING kind, which the task file allowed): SXML_RESOURCE_KIND_COLLATION_DATA also names urn:sxml:collation-data: + a path under CLDR's common/, as 's urn:sxml:timezone-data: names zoneinfo paths: uca/allkeys_CLDR.txt (the root table) and collation/<locale>.xml (a language's LDML file). processor.h says so (comments only). sxml builds the paths from ASCII letters, digits, _ and /, so a host maps them onto a CLDR checkout. The CLDR files are the data, as CLDR publishes them; nothing is converted or compiled into sxml.

The root is CLDR's (UTS #35, Part 5, section 3.1): the feature asks for allkeys_CLDR.txt first and for 's DUCET only when that is not served (hosts that serve only the DUCET keep working). The two differ in U+FFFE (lowest primary) and U+FFFF (highest), Tibetan contractions (which give the same results under sxml's longest match), and the variable marks (CLDR marks only space and punctuation). With the CLDR root, maxVariable's groups are CLDR's reorder groups space, punct, symbol and currency; with the DUCET, 's marks and categories (so CollationTest's SHIFTED sample still passes). A file without @implicitweights (allkeys_CLDR.txt has none) gets UTS #10 16.0.0's Tangut, Nushu and Khitan ranges.

Tailorings (glossary ; src/collation_tailoring.c): a tailoring is a table of the same form over its parent; lookups walk the chain to the root. Its weights are the root's shifted left 8 bits plus an offset per level, so 255 tailored weights fit after each root weight (the element struct grows from 6 to 10 bytes). Each relation puts a node after the last element of the reset position, past the nodes of weaker strength already there (ICU's order: &a<b then &a<<c gives a << c < b); when the rules are read, the lists are walked to give the offsets. The case of a tailored element is that of the first character of its string with a primary weight. Strings are put into NFD; input is always NFD, so canonically equivalent strings match.

Rule syntax (UTS #35, Part 5, sections 3.3 to 3.12): resets, < << <<< = and their starred lists with ranges, extensions /, quotes, \u \U (unescaped before parsing, as ICU's resource compiler does: en_US_POSIX quotes ' '), \x{}, # comments, and the settings strength, alternate, backwards 2, caseLevel, caseFirst, maxVariable, numericOrdering, normalization, reorder and import (read with an explicit stack of rule texts, ). Not supported, so the collation is not honoured: [before n], special reset positions ([first variable], [last tertiary ignorable]), prefixes x|y, quaternary relations, [suppressContractions], [optimize]. That leaves out root's search, eor and emoji types and what imports them (de's search and eor); private-unihan has no data here.

Settings and URI parameters: a tailoring's settings apply to the parameters the URI does not set (sxml_collation.explicit_parameters); fr-CA's [backwards 2] gives QT4 UCA-misc-lang-003 its -1, and backwards=no in the URI still wins.

Languages (F&O 4.0, 5.2.4 lang; UTS #35, Part 1, section 3): the tag is read without case, _ or -; the locale is looked up by truncation (de_AT, de, then root) and the type is standard, the file's defaultCollation, or the -u-co- keyword (BCP 47 aliases phonebk, trad, dict, gb2312); other extensions and keywords are not honoured. A language whose files have no collation of the default type is the root order and honoured when a file of the language (not root) is served; one without files, or a type no file has, is not honoured: the root order with fallback=yes, FOCH0002 and XQST0038 with fallback=no. en, en-XX and und still need no data ().

Reordering (UTS #35, Part 5, section 3.13; glossary ): src/collation_tables.c, generated by tools/generate-collation-tables.py from CLDR's FractionalUCA_SHORT.txt (not vendored; its hash is in the file and the README), lists 170 groups in root order by their first code point (Han and the unassigned code points by their implicit weights); the root table finds where each starts. Codes are compared without case; special groups not named stay first, then the named ones, others/Zzzz standing for the rest (at the end when absent); default alone is none. Scripts that CLDR puts at one weight move together (Hira Kana, Merc Mero), as do Hani Hans Hant. Separators: comma, space, hyphen.

Kept: per processor, up to 64 tailorings by key (the tag and the reorder codes, lower case), with the answer "not honoured" too, so a query cannot grow the state; past 64 a new key is not honoured. Malformed CLDR data makes a language not honoured; allocator and resolver failures are returned and nothing is kept.

Vendored (, ): third_party/cldr (CLDR 47, tag release-47), common/uca/allkeys_CLDR.txt and common/collation/ root, en, en_US, en_US_POSIX, de, de_AT, es, fr, fr_CA, it, nl, with LICENSE, README and hashes; third_party/cldr.version. 2.3 MB, nearly all the root.

Hosts: the QT4 driver serves ../cldr/common/PATH from the catalog for the URN (the XSLT driver forwards to the same table, so it serves the CLDR root and the tailorings; xsl:sort lang="es" sorts ñ after nz); the unit tests read the vendored files. The sxml command embeds allkeys_CLDR.txt (comments stripped) and the LDML files but root.xml, and serves them by path (it no longer embeds the DUCET); sxml xpath, xquery and transform have lang, reorder and xsl:sort lang (tests cli/xpath_uca_tailoring, cli/transform_sort_lang). The JavaScript package is unchanged: its default data is still the DUCET (the root falls back to it), and a host resolver can answer the urn:sxml:collation-data: paths as 'collation-data'.

Measured (release drivers): QT4 XQ40 and XP40 over the collation sets (fn-compare, fn-contains, fn-starts-with, fn-ends-with, the four fn-substring sets, fn-collation-key, fn-collation, fn-collation-available, fn-deep-equal, prod-GroupByClause, prod-OrderByClause, prod-DefaultCollationDecl, app-spec-examples, misc-UCACollation, fn-sort, fn-distinct-values, fn-index-of, fn-max, fn-min, fn-default-collation) unchanged on the CLDR root, no case lost; UCA-misc-lang-003 (fr-CA) passes by the tailoring now instead of by FOCH0002, and lang=de, fr and nl with fallback=no are supported. XT40 collations 39 of 43, sort 82 of 83, merge, for-each-group, avt, function, choose, error, maps, capture, json-to-xml, xsl-document, docbook unchanged (their lang sorts are built to sort the same in any language); a scratch XT40 case shows xsl:sort lang="es" through the XSLT driver. Unit tests: tests/collation_uca_test.c 11 cases (3 new).

Sizes (wasm preset, stripped / gzip -9, before and after this packet at one HEAD): sxml.wasm 2,135,848 / 731,180 to 2,136,223 / 731,851 (+375: the resolution of lang and reorder); sxml-full.wasm 6,794,049 / 1,495,370 to 6,819,175 / 1,504,932 (+25,126, the tailoring code and the reorder groups); the CLI module 8,495,567 / 1,883,993 to 8,532,870 / 1,900,382 (+37,303: the code and 12 KB of LDML; the CLDR root replaces the DUCET at the same size). All within 's budgets (2,200,000 / 770,000; 7,000,000 / 2,450,000; 9,000,000 / 2,000,000).

Left (for 7.17 and later): the rule syntax above that is not supported (it would add the search, eor and emoji types, and Japanese and Chinese tailorings, which also need prefixes and [before n]); other languages are data only (a host serves their CLDR files). For 7.17: third_party/cldr is the place for CLDR's main/ and rbnf/ files of the same languages (same release, README, hashes), and the urn:sxml: + CLDR path scheme, the locale truncation and the LDML reading of src/collation_tailoring.c are the patterns to reuse (lifting them into a shared module when a second user exists).
